header: THE SAME PHOTOGRAPH UNDER TWO ADDRESSES. One press photo (a meeting at a steel plant) reaches the cards from two papers, each with its own copy of the picture, so the addresses differ and rss.ts's samePictureStory cannot see that it is one picture. For the few pairs of stories whose headlines share three words or more and whose picture addresses differ, I make a small fingerprint of each picture (a "difference hash": the picture shrunk to 9 x 8 grey squares, one bit for whether each square is brighter than its right neighbour; 64 bits) and call the two the same photograph when at most MAX_DIFFERENT bits differ. A copy that was resized or recompressed differs in a few bits; a different photograph of the same plant in many. Both conditions must hold (words and photograph), so two different stories that share a stock picture, or two photographs of one company, are not joined. Only pictures on the allowed hosts are fetched, with a time limit and a size ceiling, as the thumbnail route does.

symbols.name: LOGO_WHITE
doc: A picture that is at least this much near-white (every colour 235 or more of 255) is a logo or a flat graphic, not a photograph of the story: measured 28 Nov 2026, Dainik Bhaskar's logo 93%; real photographs of the Steel tab, even with white margins, 17% to 67%.

symbols.name: isInspected
doc: Has this picture been looked at (and read) already? Only such a picture may be shown: the owner's rule is no logo, ever, so a picture that could not be looked at in time is not shown until it has been.

symbols.name: rejectLogos
symbols.sig: export async function rejectLogos(images: Array<string | undefined>, ms = 2500): Promise<number>
doc: THE OWNER'S RULE, NO RELEVANT PICTURE, NO STORY: looks at the pictures of a list and rejects the ones that are logos (rejectPicture, so that usableImage says no from now on and the next build drops those stories). A paper's logo is what an image search gives for a story it has no picture of (Dainik Bhaskar's, on a Steel story). Within `ms`; a picture that cannot be read is left as it is. Returns how many were newly rejected.

symbols.name: dropSamePhoto
symbols.sig: export async function dropSamePhoto<T extends FeedItem>(items: T[], ms = 2500, maxPairs = 8, hashOfAddress: (u: string) => Promise<bigint | null> = photoHash): Promise<T[]>
doc: Leaves each photograph once: of two stories whose headlines share three words or more and whose pictures are the same photograph (a fingerprint within MAX_DIFFERENT bits), the first in the list stays and names the other paper. At most `maxPairs` pairs are looked at, within `ms` milliseconds; a picture that cannot be read counts as different (the story stays).
